extracted.intended_audience: users of Metapost / mplib and LuaLaTeX (TeX users wanting example drawings and source)
extracted.subtask_description: A GitHub README describing a collection of Metapost + mplib example documents and drawings, their source structure, required dependencies, viewing/building options, and auxiliary files/scripts. Intended to teach drawing techniques and show reproducible examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: License / permitted use
rubrics_metrics.description: My TeX / Metapost source files are covered by the GNU Public License V3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This means you can use them for any non-commercial purpose. The documents are strictly for educational and tutorial purposes only. All the original books and therefore all the pictures are copyrighted by the Mathematical Association of America.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required packages and fonts
rubrics_metrics.description: You will also need the metapost-colorbrewer package installed (this is part of any full TeX distribution), and the TeX Gyre Pagella and TeX Gyre Pagella Math fonts installed and available to fontspec.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your TeX distribution includes metapost-colorbrewer and that fontspec can locate the TeX Gyre Pagella fonts before compiling the examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build environment (LuaLaTeX + mplib)
rubrics_metrics.description: The intent is to provide a tutorial to drawing with plain Metapost, as well as to show what can be done with mplib and lualatex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The source of each PDF file is a single TeX file with each drawing as a separate mplib environment. The examples rely on running LuaLaTeX (with mplib) to produce the PDFs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source file structure / external MP modules
rubrics_metrics.description: The files use a few external Metapost files, that include: arrow_label.mp, isometric-projection.mp, mark_equal.mp, markle.mp, paintball.mp, thatch.mp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These external files provide reusable drawing utilities (e.g., arrow_label.mp draws a double arrow with a label in the middle; isometric-projection.mp for simple 3D; mark_equal.mp draws equal-line pecks; markle.mp draws angle marks; paintball.mp draws slightly-solid balls; thatch.mp a simple hatching routine). Keep these modules available in the expected paths when compiling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing options for outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: You can view each document in three ways: admire the PDF versions; open the corresponding TeX file and browse the source and the corresponding PDF output side by side; or read the 'parallel' versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The parallel versions show MP source on the left and the MP image on the right of each double page spread; these parallel PDFs are probably best viewed on a large screen with a PDF viewer that lets you show two pages side by side. Code colouring is done using the included dwmpcode.sty style file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallel-code generation script constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The parallel versions are generated from the same LuaLaTeX source files by the Python script duplicate_mplibcode_as_examples.py.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This script is not very general; it depends on the particular structure used for these documents. Expect it to work only with similarly-structured source files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance / compile-time expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document contains over 100 fairly complex Metapost drawings, and on my Mac Mini (M2 2023) it takes about 4 seconds to compile each one, or roughly 25-30 full page drawings per second.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compile times will vary by machine; use this as a rough benchmark for performance when running the examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and provenance of the drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: PWW-1 and PWW-2 are attempts to re-draw some of the drawings from Roger Nelsen's 'Proofs without words' books; Excursions has drawings and notes inspired by Stanley Ogilvie's 'Excursions in Geometry'; Cosmopolitan Tiling presents many tiling examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents are educational/tutorial recreations and include minimal notes on techniques. Because the originals are copyrighted, the examples are presented for study rather than for republishing the source material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to ask questions / community support
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have questions about Metapost or any of my examples, please consider asking them on a Q&A site like http://tex.stackexchange.com/ using the metapost tag.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer asking on the public TeX StackExchange using the metapost tag rather than contacting the repo owner directly for general help.
